classification.difficultyReason: Requires identifying congruent complementary regions and combining overlapping sectors with an equilateral triangle to obtain an exact area.

inlines.text: Give your answer as an exact value.

spec.description: Upright unit square containing four corner-centred quarter-circle arcs. The central region and four corner regions are shaded; four regions adjoining the side midpoints are white.
spec.mathematics: Square vertices are (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (0,1). Each arc has radius 1 and its centre at a square vertex. The two arcs from the bottom corners intersect at (1/2, sqrt(3)/2); the other intersections follow by square symmetry.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given side length 1 and the requested shaded regions are visible.

inlines.text: Subtract four congruent white regions from the unit square, using sector areas and an equilateral triangle.

answer.worked:
Let $A$ and $B$ be the bottom corners and $E$ the upper intersection of their quarter-circle arcs. Since $AB=AE=BE=1$, triangle $ABE$ is equilateral.

The overlap area $Q$ of these two quarter disks is the sum of two sectors with angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$, less triangle $ABE$:
$$\begin{align*}Q&=2\left(\frac12\times1^2\times\frac{\pi}{3}\right)-\frac12\times1\times1\times\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\\Q&=\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}.\end{align*}$$
The white region $W$ adjoining the top side is the square less the union of the two quarter disks:
$$\begin{align*}W&=1-\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{4}-Q\right)\\W&=1-\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}.\end{align*}$$
The four white regions are congruent. Hence the shaded area is
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{shaded}}&=1-4W\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=1-4\left(1-\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\right)\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=\sqrt3+\frac{2\pi}{3}-3.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unit square showing the two bottom-corner quarter disks, their overlap Q and the equilateral triangle ABE.
spec.mathematics: A=(0,0), B=(1,0), E=(1/2,sqrt(3)/2). All three triangle sides have length 1. Q is the upper half of the lens formed by the two unit disks.
